problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $26{x}_{1},$ where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-18 \\ 27\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

examples.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the vector $\mathbf{x}$ below, find the value of $x_2,$ the second component of $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}.$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066805/assets/4f788e589f34c94ac03e11f7cee87f9af695af2a86d57a2e4630f07c30babb1e.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2,\,\mathbf{q}_3.$ 

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066805/assets/cfa33ba159e0627ec7a7288e44249acd88e0037e285fa786888dfcc13e5d538c.png) where $x_i = \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}{\mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}.$ 

Computing $x_2,$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{2}}{{q}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 1+6\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-4)}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4+6+8}{1+1+16} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
